rationale: Both lanes identify the identical defect and mechanism: after the JSON-schema grammar terminates, the model emits an Inkling block-terminator special token (200028, <|end_message|>/content_model_end_sampling), the scheduler still force-feeds it to grammar.accept_tokens with no is_terminated() guard, xgrammar returns False via `if self._is_terminated: return False`, and the scheduler mis-reads that False as a fatal rejection -> FINISHED_ERROR -> 500. Both cite the same load-bearing lines (backend_xgrammar.py:157-171, scheduler.py:1829-1855, should_advance latching reasoning_ended) and both refute the 'disallowed/above-vocab token' symptom theory. Their primary fix is the same (guard the scheduler accept_tokens call with grammar.is_terminated(), plus have xgrammar return True post-termination), so both would let the failing input finish normally; the differences (Lane A's full-mask unconstraining insight vs Lane B's cross-backend corroboration from guidance/outlines and two-terminator wire-format analysis) are complementary refinements, not contradictions. Neither diagnosis dominates the other in correctness or completeness, hence tie; aligned on root_cause so advance the phase.
